title: Plot size and shape from a uniformity trial
text: criterion locates one point fitted surface closed-form solution: max_gaussian_curvature(): point maximum Gaussian curvature surface. simultaneous_sectional_curvature(): point CV curve along width CV curve along length reach maximum curvature. direction reproduces classical modified maximum-curvature method. marginal_efficiency_2d(): point one basic unit width, length, reduces CV target_slope percentage points. three points lie close together surface, correspond different plot areas.
code: rbind(   max_gaussian_curvature(surface$a, surface$m, surface$n),   simultaneous_sectional_curvature(surface$a, surface$m, surface$n),   marginal_efficiency_2d(surface$a, surface$m, surface$n, target_slope = 1) ) #>   criterion    width   length     area       cv          K #> 1  gaussian 4.335096 1.448599 6.279817 8.631981 0.02558784 #> 2 sectional 4.599877 1.542882 7.097068 8.205307 0.02535289 #> 3  marginal 4.730074 1.805704 8.541114 7.777921 0.02394040 plot(result) plot(result, which = "sections")

text: package includes four uniformity trials Guanacaste, Costa Rica: rice maize (20 x 20 basic units) Nambí common bean cowpea (10 x 20 basic units). vignette walks complete analysis: vignette("plotsizing"). analyse trial, save yields CSV one column per field column, header row row-number column: unit_width_m unit_length_m give physical size one basic unit used convert results metres.

title: Experimental Unit Dimensions from Bivariate CV Surfaces
text: CV surface CV(x,y)=ax−−nCV(x, y) = \, x^{-m} y^{-n} fitted nonlinear least squares, x plot width y plot length basic units, CV percent. Three criteria available, closed-form solution: "gaussian": point maximum Gaussian curvature surface. "sectional": point CV curves along width along length reach maximum curvature, two-dimensional version modified maximum-curvature method. "marginal": point CV decreases target_slope percentage points per additional basic unit, along width along length. package also fits Smith (1938) variance law weighted least squares (weights M - 1, free intercept) enumerates every exact rectangular partition trial least two plots. calculations use basic-unit coordinates CV percent. results depend choice scale, target_slope marginal criterion, continuous solutions compared plot configurations feasible field.

title: Experimental Unit Dimensions from Bivariate CV Surfaces
text: plot(result, = ...) draws "contours", "surface", "sections", "profiles" "heatmap". underlying functions can also called directly:
code: cfg <- result$configurations surface <- result$surface  plot_trial_heatmap(trial) plot_cv_profiles(cfg, surface) plot_cv_contours(surface, cfg) plot_cv_surface(surface, cfg) plot_curvature_sections(surface, criterion = "all", configurations = cfg) plot_multicrop_curvature()

title: Experimental-unit dimensions by two-dimensional marginal efficiency — marginal_efficiency_2d
text: marginal decreases surface \(-\partial CV / \partial x = m\,CV / x\) \(-\partial CV / \partial y = n\,CV / y\). Setting equal target_slope yields unique positive solution closed form \(x = (\,m^{\,n+1} / (\tau\,n^{n}))^{1/(m+n+1)}\), \(y = (\,n^{\,m+1} / (\tau\,m^{m}))^{1/(m+n+1)}\) length--width ratio \(n/m\). marginal criterion coordinates, geometric-curvature criterion, result depends scale coefficient variation dimensions expressed; computation basic units physical conversion applied afterwards.
